items.title: Measuring AI innovation with trademark data
items.desc: Proposes using trademark records as a novel data source to map the development and diffusion of artificial intelligence across firms and industries, complementing patent- and publication-based measures. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-21]

items.title: Curriculum design in the age of AI
items.desc: Develops a learning-by-doing model in which a myopic student can work on tasks or delegate them to AI, and uses it to study how AI adoption reshapes skill formation and optimal curriculum design. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-07-21]

items.title: Prediction of bank transaction fraud using TabNet, an adaptive deep learning architecture
items.desc: Applies TabNet, an interpretable deep-learning architecture for tabular data, to detect fraudulent online banking transactions, emphasizing scalability and explainability for real-world financial fraud prevention. [arXiv q-fin.GN, posted 2026-07-21]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: America’s AI labs are under threat from cheap Chinese rivals
items.desc: The Economist argues that lower-cost Chinese AI models are eroding the pricing power and competitive edge of leading U.S. AI labs, with significant implications for the economics of the AI industry. [Economist, 2026-07-21]

items.title: Will the U.S. and China Build Walls Around A.I.?
items.desc: NYT DealBook examines the escalating U.S.–China contest over AI export controls and market access, and what a more fragmented, bloc-based AI economy could mean for firms and investors. [NYT DealBook, 2026-07-21]
